newsitem.title: UK: OPEC ECB sees '97 call on OPEC crude at 25.2 mbpd.
newsitem.headline: OPEC ECB sees '97 call on OPEC crude at 25.2 mbpd.

text.p: OPEC's Economic Commission Board (ECB) of market and technical experts from all 11 members forecast 1997 demand for OPEC crude oil at 25.2 million barrels per day (bpd) at a meeting in Vienna, an ECB delegate said on Thursday.
The ECB, which also forecast world demand of 70.8 million bpd, was meeting to prepare a 1997 oil supply-demand outlook ahead of next week's full ministerial conference.
"Everbody agreed the figures," the delegate told Reuters by telephone from Vienna.
The ECB's figures compare with last month's OPEC Secretariat report which estimated 1996 demand for OPEC crude at 25 million bpd and forecast only modest growth to 25.08 million in 1997.
The Secretariat has also forecast 1997 world oil demand at 70.63 million bpd in its September report.

The ECB report, along with a market study prepared by the Secretariat will be used by ministers when they meet on November 27 in Vienna to set production levels for the cartel for the first half of 1997.
Despite high oil prices, OPEC is not expected to tamper with its 25.03 million bpd ceiling agreed at its June ministerial conference, OPEC delegates and ministerial sources say.
Less than a week before the start of the biannual talks, OPEC ministers show no sign they plan to boost output to take advantage of the prolonged rally.
"Don't rock the boat should be our motto at this meeting," said a delegate from an OPEC Gulf member.
